A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E-mem study and contain complete, readable main text and appendices A–L. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables and prompts.

before.justification: v2 reports original LoCoMo and HotpotQA experiments, ablations and runtime measurements, plus AMA evaluation and additional robustness results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark and appendix experiments, revises several reported scores, and provides a replacement cost–latency comparison.

M1.justification: The master–assistant architecture, overlapping memory segmentation, three routing pathways, temporal anchoring and response generation are unchanged. Algorithm 1, the routing implementation in Appendix I and the prompts in Appendix L are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LoCoMo, HotpotQA at 400/800/1600 documents and AMA's six domains. Adversarial queries, continuous memory without resetting and shuffled document order already appear in v2. The revised efficiency comparison introduces no identifiable new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 9's efficiency comparison adds RAG and drops A-mem and MemoryOS, retaining Mem0, LightMem and GAM. Other comparison sets are unchanged; AriGraph, HippoRAG and the stronger long-context models were already evaluated in v2.

E3.justification: Table 9 replaces separate memory-building, reasoning and total runtimes at two HotpotQA scales with a single per-query latency measure alongside F1 and cost. The replacement timing setup is not fully specified, preventing direct comparison of the old and new latency values. Main benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B replaces the analysis of runtime components across HotpotQA scales with a joint accuracy–cost–latency analysis. The existing model, routing, chunk-size, direct-read, continuous-memory, document-ordering and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without specifying repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Revisions include direct-read overall F1 from 39.71 to 38.27 (Table 6), no-reset F1 from 52.65 to 51.75 (Table 8), GPT-5.1 overall F1 from 53.31 to 52.31 (Appendix D), and HippoRAG overall F1 from 47.81 to 46.91 (Appendix E), plus smaller Mem0, AriGraph and chunk-ablation updates. Section 4.2 changes the HotpotQA-1600 margin from 7.29 to 6.51 points, matching the unchanged Qwen2.5-14B results. Table 9 replaces the old runtimes with new latency results, including 11.25 seconds for E-mem. Headline E-mem accuracy results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the segmentation and activation definitions, the O(1) update assertion and Appendix I's routing normalization remain unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about episodic context reconstruction, heterogeneous collaboration, superior benchmark performance and reduced token cost. Appendix B's revised discussion does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B drops the argument that construction savings amortize higher inference latency over lifelong operation. It instead explains the trade-off through normalized cost and per-query latency, with an explicit qualification that E-mem is not a universal replacement for fast retrieval systems. The broader latency–fidelity discussion remains in Appendix J.

D1.justification: The disclosed GPUs, model configurations, embedding models, routing procedure, storage requirements, optional KV caching and prompts remain unchanged. Code and data access information is also retained; the replacement timing results do not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: v5 adds an AriGraph bibliographic citation and explicit graph-baseline citations in Appendix E. HippoRAG was already referenced in v2, while the removed AIOS preprint entry represents the same work retained through its publication entry. The substantive related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix B is locally rewritten, acknowledgements are added, and author order, affiliations, correspondence details and running headers are revised. The main narrative and appendix organization remain stable. Appendix J.1's previously valid Table 9 reference becomes 'Table??'.

P2.justification: Table 9 is redesigned from a phase-by-scale runtime table into method rows with F1, cost and latency columns, with a new caption. Other figures and table structures are retained, accompanied by modest text reflow and spacing changes.

improvement.justification: v5 corrects the HotpotQA margin and offers a useful joint cost–latency comparison, but weakens reporting consistency. Mem0 BLEU-1 is now 35.08 in Table 1 versus 34.92 in Table 7; RAG cost differs without explanation between Tables 9 and 7 (4,590 versus 6,430). The revision also removes the detailed HotpotQA runtime breakdown and breaks Appendix J.1's table reference. These limited losses in the clarity and checkability of the evidence outweigh the localized clarification and citation gains.
